lead: A `loop-goal.toml` program check runs its `file` through `leg.run`, which prepends `run`, so reproducing one by hand as `nvs <file>` answers `unrecognized subcommand` and reads as a misfiled check.
body: Every `exact`, `ordered`, `contains` and `min-bytes` check in the list omits `args` for exactly that reason (`tools/loop.py:1449`), so a missing `args = ["run"]` is never what is wrong with a red one. Reproduce a program check as `target/debug/nvs.exe run <file>` and judge stdout alone — `exact` compares `stdout_lines` and never reads stderr, so a fixture whose stderr is full of warnings can still be green.
